$comment: The repository-wide ledger of deprecated symbols (TASK-S2-O2). packages/contracts/VERSIONING.md §4 says in so many words that this file did not exist -- 'There is no repository-wide ledger of deprecated symbols. Three partial ones exist ... Nothing records a deprecated *prop*, *part* or *state*. That gap is recorded, not closed here.' This closes it. Data, not code: deprecating one more symbol is an edit HERE plus the `@deprecated` annotation, and `yarn validate:deprecations` fails if either exists without the other.
$whyHereAndNotInSrc: The records sit at packages/contracts/deprecations.json, NOT under packages/contracts/src/. `files` for @dzup-ui/contracts is ["LICENSE","VERSIONING.md","dist"], so a root-level data file changes no published tarball and adds no symbol to a types-only package's public surface. Putting the record TYPE in contracts/src would have added an export to a published package in the middle of a release candidate, which is a publication act this task has no authority for. The type therefore lives with the validator, in packages/tooling/src/validators/deprecations.ts, and is re-stated here as $recordShape. See TASK-S2-O2 handoff D-S2O2-4.

$recordShape.symbol: the deprecated name as a consumer writes it -- a component, a function, a prop path (`Interface.prop`), a module specifier, or a CSS custom property
$recordShape.package: the published package name that ships it
$recordShape.annotation: { file, anchor? } -- the `@deprecated` JSDoc this record accounts for. `anchor` is a literal substring that must appear within `annotationWindow` lines AFTER the annotation; it is required only when a file carries more than one annotation.
$recordShape.replacement: the named replacement a consumer moves to. Never null: VERSIONING.md §4 requires one.
$recordShape.replacementExample: a one-line before/after a reader can copy
$recordShape.firstDeprecated: the package version in which the annotation first appeared, DERIVED from git (`git log -S'@deprecated' --reverse -- <file>`, then the package.json version at that commit), not typed by hand
$recordShape.firstDeprecatedBasis: the commit the version was derived from, or why it could not be
$recordShape.earliestRemoval: the earliest version in which the symbol may be removed. VERSIONING.md §4: at least one full 0.x minor series, removed in a MINOR.
$recordShape.earliestRemovalBasis: why that version and not another -- a policy citation, not a preference
$recordShape.codemod: a transform id under packages/codemods/src/transforms/<id>.ts, or null
$recordShape.codemodGap: when `codemod` is non-null but does not perform the whole migration, what it leaves to the reader. Omitted when the codemod is complete.
$recordShape.migration: required when `codemod` is null -- VERSIONING.md §4 allows 'written instructions where it is not [mechanical]', and this is where they are named
$recordShape.runtimeWarning: { status: present | absent | not-applicable, mechanism, evidence, reason }. doc 06 says 'runtime development warning WHEN PRACTICAL', so `absent` and `not-applicable` are conformant -- but only with a reason. A missing reason is a validator failure.
$recordShape.rollback: what a consumer does if the replacement does not work for them
$recordShape.docs: the document a reader is sent to

$rules.proseRule: An `@deprecated` wrapped in backticks is PROSE (a document describing the tag), not an annotation. Three such mentions exist at 4e4e46f -- packages/tokens/src/dtcg.ts (×2, the doc comment on DEPRECATED_TOKENS) and packages/tooling/src/meta/component-meta.ts (×1, the doc comment on the `deprecated` field). Stripping inline-code spans before the match separates them mechanically, so no allowlist is needed and no future prose mention has to be hand-registered.
$rules.bijection: Every annotation must be claimed by exactly one record and every record must claim exactly one annotation. Both directions are failures: `annotated without a record` and `record without an annotation`.
$rules.removalOverdue: A record whose `earliestRemoval` is <= the package's CURRENT version while the symbol is still annotated is a failure -- the deprecation window has closed and nothing acted on it.
$rules.codemodExists: A non-null `codemod` must name a file that exists at packages/codemods/src/transforms/<id>.ts.
$rules.reasonRequired: `runtimeWarning.status` of `absent` or `not-applicable` requires a non-empty `reason`; `codemod: null` requires `migration`.

$partialLedgersThisSupersedes: packages/tooling/scripts/retired-package-names.json -- package NAMES only, 1 entry. Still authoritative for its own question; not a symbol ledger.

DEPRECATED_TOKENS in packages/tokens/src/dtcg.ts -- 2 entries, the two sidebar aliases below. It lifts `$deprecated` into the DTCG export and its own doc comment says it 'CAN fall behind a newly deprecated token'. Both of its entries now also appear here.
`@deprecated` JSDoc on the compat adapters -- 11 entries, all below.
